oneLiner: The enterprise software franchise that became the second-largest AI cloud, where the market is betting that Azure's 40%+ growth and Copilot attach outrun the depreciation of a capex budget now above a third of revenue. The stock works if operating margin bends but does not break.
thesis: Azure is accelerating at $100B+ scale. Management guided first-half FY27 acceleration (Q1 ~45% cc) with demand still above capacity; the new Azure revenue disclosure from Q1 FY27 removes the main reason to discount the number.
Contracted demand de-risks the buildout. Commercial RPO of $678B (+84% YoY) still grows ~25% excluding OpenAI, so most of the capacity being built is pre-sold to a broad base.
Copilot is an option on 464M seats. 30M+ paid M365 Copilot seats is ~6.5% penetration; each additional 10M seats at list price is roughly $3.6B of annual revenue at software margins.

Margin discipline under load. FY27 guide calls for double-digit operating income growth with opex up only mid-to-high single digits and margin down less than 1pt - the cost base is being held while depreciation rises.
Model optionality. A ~25-27% as-converted OpenAI stake (sources differ), a $3.2B Anthropic gain in Q4 FY26 and in-house MAI models reduce single-lab dependence.

latestQuarter.label: Q4 FY2026 (ended Jun 30, 2026; reported Jul 29, 2026)
points: Revenue $90.0B, +18% YoY (+17% cc) vs ~$87.6B consensus; FY26 revenue $331.8B, net income $133.7B.
Azure +43% (first $100B+ fiscal year, +41% in FY26); Microsoft Cloud $59.3B (+27%).
Operating income $40.6B, margin 45.1% (48.9% in Q1 FY26); GAAP EPS $4.81, non-GAAP $4.74 - GAAP includes a $3.2B Anthropic investment gain.
Capex $35.8B of PP&E purchases (~$41B as reported including finance leases; split unverified); FY26 cash capex $115.9B; Q4 FCF $19.6B.

segments: From Q1 FY27 Microsoft reports two segments (8-K, Sep 2026): Agents and Infra (Azure, M365 commercial and consumer, server, GitHub, industry solutions, enterprise services) and Devices and Consumer (Windows OEM and devices, Xbox, LinkedIn, search advertising).
Recast Q4 FY26 Azure revenue $29.4B, +42% YoY; one summary says the new definition is narrower (GitHub cloud, Security Copilot, health cloud moved out) - unverified against the 8-K.
Old-basis Q4 FY26 mix: Intelligent Cloud $39.3B (+32%), Productivity & Business Processes $37.8B (+14%), More Personal Computing $12.9B (-4%).
competitive: Cloud infrastructure share (Q1 2026): AWS ~30%, Azure ~25%, Google Cloud ~13%; Azure grows fastest of the three, but AWS reaccelerated to 37% in Q2 2026.
Copilot vs Google Workspace/Gemini in productivity AI; GitHub Copilot (50M users) vs Cursor, Claude Code and other coding agents.
OpenAI is partner, tenant, investee and rival - exclusivity ended and revenue-share economics were restructured in Oct 2025 and Apr 2026; OpenAI now buys compute from AWS, Oracle and CoreWeave too.
Model hedges: Anthropic models in Copilot and Foundry, in-house MAI models (three released since Oct 1, 2026).
moat: Enterprise distribution: ~464M M365 commercial seats, identity/Teams lock-in and compliance-grade trust let Microsoft attach AI to workflows it already owns. $678B of contracted RPO plus a capacity base that added 88 data centers in FY26 gives demand visibility and scale economics only AWS can rival.
risks: Depreciation eats the margin. Operating margin fell from 48.9% to 45.1% over the last four quarters as capex reached 34.9% of TTM revenue (13.3% in FY2023); the FY27 guide (down <1pt) leaves little room if Azure gross margin slips.
Free cash flow lags earnings. FY26 FCF of $67.0B was half of net income after $115.9B of cash capex, and FY27 capex grows again - FCF stays flat until the buildout pays back.
OpenAI concentration and circularity. $24.1B of FY26 revenue came from one loss-making customer; RPO grows 84% with OpenAI and ~25% without, and OpenAI equity-method results swing GAAP EPS.

Accounting optics. Extending data-center useful lives from 15 to 25 years moves new leases from finance to operating, lowering reported capex and deferring depreciation with no change in spend - and the new segment/Azure definitions break comparisons just as growth is judged.
Copilot could stall at shallow penetration. ~6.5% of the base three years after launch; usage-based GitHub billing since June 2026 flatters reported growth.
catalysts: Oct 28, 2026 (after close): Q1 FY27 report - first under two segments with Azure in dollars; Azure vs 44-45% cc guide, operating margin, capex vs >$50B guide, ex-OpenAI RPO (debates 1, 2, 3).
Nov 17, 2026: Nadella Financial Community Briefing alongside Ignite (Nov 17-20, San Francisco) - Copilot pricing and agent roadmap (debate 1).
~Late Jan 2027: Q2 FY27 report - whether first-half Azure acceleration held and the FY27 margin guide is reaffirmed (debates 1, 2).
Ongoing: OpenAI funding, compute contracts and any IPO step, which move RPO and equity-method results (debate 3).

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings: FY26 cash capex of $115.9B compresses FCF well below earnings power, and the useful-life accounting change muddies cash-flow comparability.

latestProse: Q4 FY26 (ended Jun 30; reported Jul 29): revenue $90.0B (+18%), GAAP net income $35.8B (+31%), GAAP EPS $4.81 including a $3.2B Anthropic gain, non-GAAP $4.74 vs ~$4.24 expected. Azure grew 43% and crossed $100B for the fiscal year; Microsoft Cloud reached $59.3B (+27%). Operating margin was 45.1%, the fourth straight quarterly decline from 48.9% in Q1 FY26, as depreciation from the buildout lands. FY26 closed at $331.8B revenue and $133.7B net income, with $115.9B of cash capex and $67.0B of FCF. Commercial RPO reached $678B; Microsoft did not refresh its April AI run-rate figure.
guidanceProse: Q1 FY27 guide: revenue $89.85-90.95B (+16-17%), Azure +44-45% cc, capex above $50B including the lease reclassification. Recast into the new segments (Sep 8-K): Agents and Infra $75.15-75.75B, Devices and Consumer $14.7-15.2B. FY27: double-digit revenue and operating income growth, opex up mid-to-high single digits, operating margin down less than 1pt, FCF positive, first-half Azure acceleration. FY27 capex grows YoY; summaries put it at ~$175B, but whether that figure is FY27 or calendar 2026 differs by source (unverified), and the $255-260B figure quoted in July is an analyst estimate. Pre-print consensus: EPS ~$4.73, revenue ~$90.65B; a sub-45% Azure print is the widely cited disappointment line.

verdict.summary: MSFT is the most diversified way to own the AI buildout: Azure growth is accelerating, RPO still grows ~25% excluding OpenAI, and the rest of the franchise funds the spend. The quality check's two flags - a 4pt operating margin slide and capex at 34.9% of revenue - are the real debate, and management's FY27 guide (margin down <1pt) is the line to hold. The base case returns low-double digits with ~22% downside in the bear; the view turns cautious if Azure misses its 44-45% guide or if margin guidance slips by more than a point.
wtb: Azure grows at least 40% cc in every quarter of FY27 (Q1 guide 44-45%).
FY27 operating margin stays within 1pt of FY26's 46.8% and FY28 holds ~46%, despite capex above a third of revenue.
Commercial RPO excluding OpenAI keeps growing 20%+ YoY, so the backlog is not one customer's balance sheet.
The market pays ~26x FY2028 EPS at end-2027, close to the multiple it has paid through the capex cycle.

bear.why: AI demand digests in 2027: Azure slows toward 30%, Copilot adds stall and OpenAI trims commitments; FY28 revenue grows only ~8% on ~$388B. Depreciation pushes operating margin to ~42% (net ~35%). The market prices the capex as over-built and pays a low-20s multiple.

base.why: Azure holds high-30s to 40% on contracted backlog, M365 grows mid-teens with Copilot attach: FY28 revenue +16%. Operating margin ~46%, net margin ~38.5% after ~17% tax. FCF stabilises as capex growth slows, so the multiple holds near its cycle average.

bull.why: Azure stays above 40% into FY28 and Copilot penetration doubles; revenue +21% with operating leverage returning (net ~39.5%). Visible FCF growth and a de-risked OpenAI exposure earn a high-20s multiple.

scenarioModel.note: FY27 revenue assumes ~$388B (+17%, in line with the Q1 guide). EPS = revenue x net margin / ~7.43B diluted shares (bear 420 x 35% = $147.0B; base 450 x 38.5% = $173.3B; bull 470 x 39.5% = $185.7B). EPS excludes OpenAI equity-method results and investment marks such as the Anthropic gain (non-GAAP basis), so GAAP EPS can differ by several percent in a quarter. Multiples apply to FY2028 EPS at end-2027. Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Does Azure stay above 40% as capacity lands?
debates.bull: Management guided first-half acceleration with demand above capacity; analysts (BNP) model 46% in Q1 and 49% in Q2 FY27, and Azure in dollars removes the definitional discount.
debates.bear: Some of the growth is OpenAI compute at lower margins, and OpenAI now buys from AWS, Oracle and CoreWeave; a narrower recast definition could reset the base just as growth is judged.
debates.view: Azure growth sets the multiple (21x vs 29x). We expect a print at or slightly above guide; a miss would matter more than any capex number.

signpost.metric: Azure revenue growth YoY, constant currency

debates.bull: Opex is held to mid-to-high single digits and the FY27 guide is only <1pt of margin decline; the 25-year useful life matches how long data-center shells actually last.
debates.bear: Operating margin has fallen 4pts in four quarters, capex is 34.9% of TTM revenue, and the useful-life change defers rather than removes the depreciation.
debates.view: This is the quality-check flag that matters. We accept a ~1pt decline; a second year of 2pt+ compression would move us to Cautious because it means the buildout earns below the old margin.

signpost.metric: Q1 FY27 operating margin and FY27 margin guide
signpost.threshold: bearish if Q1 margin below 45% or FY27 guide widened beyond a 1pt decline
signpost.when: Q1 FY27 report, Oct 28, 2026; reaffirm late Jan 2027

debates.q: How much of the backlog is OpenAI?
debates.bull: RPO ex-OpenAI still grows ~25%, ~90% of Microsoft Cloud comes from customers outside frontier labs, and the OpenAI stake is a large asset not in the scenarios.
debates.bear: $24.1B of FY26 revenue from one loss-making customer, and the 84% RPO headline is mostly OpenAI - if OpenAI's funding tightens, the visibility evaporates.
debates.view: A concentration risk, not the core case; it becomes one if the ex-OpenAI number decelerates while the headline holds.
